## TL;DR

The final review narrowed the remaining work to named, kind-specific skeleton counts, a rendered-count test for every kind, and one Settings contrast correction. Mission Control’s dashboard count remains exactly one. Counts are now declared in `LOADING_SKELETON_ITEM_COUNTS`, consumed by `PageSkeleton`, and checked against rendered items. The Settings description for `localChecks.reclaimGraceMs` now uses the standard muted foreground token. The two related UI test files passed, and `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed on the retry host after the first remote runner timed out.

## Work and rationale

The skeleton count map now documents each non-board kind beside its value: dashboard 1, cards 1, table 5, rows 1, targets 2, and deployments 3. Dashboard stays at one block as the owner explicitly required. One compact card is the minimal shared shape for the Agents and Releases `cards` kind; table skeletons show five compact rows; Stories and Repo context use one representative row; Dev’s target layout uses two columns; and Deployments shows three service rows. The Settings call site continues to pass `GENERAL_FIELD_SECTIONS.length`, so its six grouped sections follow the same definition as the real page. Work and Inputs retain their existing column constants.

`PageSkeleton` already reads the count map when a caller does not supply a data-derived `count`. The component test mounts every skeleton kind and checks the number of direct placeholder items against the associated map entry; board and input-board counts continue to come from their existing column constants. I replaced an obsolete assertion that required every non-board count to equal one with explicit expectations for the per-kind map. The complete component test and page-height test files then passed: 23 tests total.

The contrast issue was independent of the skeleton count changes: the Settings description uses the `--txt-faint` theme variable, which resolves to `#958ab0` on a white panel in one theme. I kept the correction local to the `localChecks.reclaimGraceMs` row and switched its description to `var(--muted-foreground)`, the existing semantic token. The rendered contrast audit passed after this change.

## Approaches tried

I first traced the failed contrast selector and confirmed this task does not change the setting’s schema description or the general `.setting-desc` color. I used a row-scoped selector to preserve other theme styling while fixing the reported combination. For the placeholder review, I discarded the pending six-block dashboard proposal, then kept a single dashboard block and moved the other defaults into the named kind map. I left board breakpoints, motion behavior, and cache seeding untouched in this final pass, consistent with the owner’s scope decision.

## Challenges and blockers

The managed ThinkPad runner timed out twice during validation. RepoOS removed the stalled validation container and retried on `bee`; that retry completed the build, all changed-path tests, rendered contrast, and UI smoke checks. An earlier suite run exposed a stale test that asserted every count was one; updating the assertion to match the named per-kind values resolved it. There are no remaining known blockers.

## Key learnings

A shared skeleton kind can serve pages with different amounts of eventual content, so the fallback should represent a realistic visible unit for that kind. Explicit per-kind constants make those decisions reviewable, while the component-level render assertion catches a mismatch between the declared count and actual markup. Contrast audits also need to cover theme combinations where a valid dark-theme muted color can land on a light panel; a semantic foreground token is safer for that row.

| Work `/work` | Status columns sharing board column constants | Same column count as the real board |
| Inputs `/inputs`, Client board | Three input-state columns | Same column count as the input board |

| Settings `/settings` | Grouped settings sections | Count from `GENERAL_FIELD_SECTIONS` |
| Repo `/repo` and detail routes | Variable documentation or detail content | One representative row |
| Check runs, reminders, schedules, providers | Variable lists inside panels | Existing table/row skeleton kinds |
